headline: High: Kestra’s broad filesystem, shell, and network defaults create dangerous interaction risks; the other profile is non-runnable and mostly inert, limiting injection and leakage pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject into B. Profile B can read files and process stdin/stdout, so if A’s content is manually copied into a workflow or file, B could misparse it as instructions. This is a limited bridge, not a default shared channel.
conditions: IF A’s output is manually pasted into a Kestra workflow or file that B reads
IF B treats file or stdin content as executable workflow instructions
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into workflow definitions
Add a review step before importing any A-generated content into B
Use a separate staging directory for imported files
Mark imported text as data, not instructions, in workflow templates

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, so it is not a meaningful leak source. B can read and write local files and egress broadly, but without a shared workspace or sensitive data in A, the pairwise leakage blast radius is small and indirect.
conditions: IF A is later connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files
IF B is granted access to data classes not currently listed for A
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Do not mount sensitive directories into B
Restrict B’s egress destinations
Audit any files copied from A before B reads them

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress, while A has no runnable or write surface. If they are co-located on the same directory or orchestration state, B can overwrite artifacts or workflow files without coordination. Uncertainty about A’s hidden runtime is not enough to lower severity.
conditions: IF A and B share a writable directory or git/workflow state
IF B runs multiple instances against the same mutable resources without locking
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory
Enable file locking or single-writer scheduling
Run B with least-privilege filesystem mounts
Use immutable artifact paths for handoffs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an inert docs-only list, so it is unlikely to generate authoritative facts. B, however, can automate downstream actions via email, Slack, PagerDuty, cloud, and SSH. If operators feed A-derived recommendations into B without verification, B can propagate mistakes into real actions. The pathway exists, but not by default.
conditions: IF A-derived text is used as an input to B’s workflow tasks
IF B is configured to send notifications or execute commands based on unverified inputs
mitigations: Require human approval before B executes actions
Add validation checks on any A-derived inputs
Log and review all outbound notifications from B
Use dry-run mode for workflows that consume A outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data classes are listed for A, so there is no documented residency or certification mismatch to escalate. B can handle logs, inputs, artifacts, database and cloud data, which creates compliance obligations, but the pairwise record does not show a conflicting regulated-data flow from A.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into B’s workflows
IF A is later used to source data subject to residency or retention rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B unless policies are documented
Set retention limits on B’s logs and artifacts
Review B’s outbound integrations before enabling them
Document data-class handling for any future A-to-B pipeline
